extracted.intended_audience: librarians and library staff (Fordham University staff and the broader library profession)
extracted.subtask_description: A curated guide to training and professional development resources for librarians, listing webinars, MOOCs, playlists, vendor training, and notes about access, intended audience, and credentials. Useful for choosing, accessing, and documenting continuing education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access requirement / login or registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Many resources require credentials or prior registration: e.g., 'Login required to view the whole tutorial.'; 'Access recorded training videos with your LibApps account credentials.'; 'Email sdsc@sirsidynix.com for help logging in.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm whether the resource requires a provider account, institutional credentials, or event registration before planning to attend or view recordings. Use provided support contacts if you cannot log in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificates of completion / professional development credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificates are available for some training: 'Certificates of completion for professional development credit will be available for download upon completion.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need PD credit, verify in advance that the training issues certificates and what steps are required to receive/download them (e.g., completing the whole tutorial).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost / free vs paid
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost varies across entries: 'Not all events are free' and several entries note 'Some content is free.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check individual provider pages to determine whether content is free, freemium, or paid; budget for paid workshops or membership-based content as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional or membership access requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Some resources are limited to institutional members or to employees: examples include 'Available to institutional members' and 'Access provided by Human Resources.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm whether access is available through your institution (HR, library subscriptions, consortium membership) before attempting to register or pay individually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource format and delivery type
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources come in multiple formats: 'Free Archived Recordings', 'Free Live Training Sites', playlists, webinars, 'MOOC', 'self-paced units', workshops, conferences, vendor trainings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose format that fits learning preferences and schedules (live interactive sessions vs. archived/on-demand vs. structured MOOCs). Note that format affects interactivity, Q&A, and certificate issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration required to view recordings
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Register for a webinar to view recording' — recordings may be gated behind event registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want access to a recording, register even if you cannot attend live; check whether registration links remain active after the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended audience / role suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Several listings indicate target learners: e.g., 'Intended for those who are converting material into alternate formats.' and 'designed specifically for public, academic or school librarians worldwide, to help them gain the knowledge and skills needed to create inclusive and accessible libraries.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select trainings targeted to your role (public/academic/school librarians, metadata staff, preservationists, etc.) to ensure relevance and appropriate depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning objectives / curriculum structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Some entries describe course structure and objectives: e.g., 'This MOOC (of 10 core modules) is designed to help equip students and researchers with the skills they need to excel in a modern research environment.'; 'RDMLA ... curriculum features 8 online self-paced units that focus on the essential knowledge and skills needed to collaborate effectively with researchers on data management.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review course modules and stated objectives to ensure alignment with your professional goals; note whether courses are self-paced, cohort-based, or module-based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access duration / time-limited availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Some resources have limited windows: 'Online educational content openly available with 2-year rolling wall.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of content access windows (rolling walls, archival limits) and download materials or complete modules before access expires if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform- or vendor-specific supports and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Many listings are provider-specific (e.g., EBSCO, ExLibris, OCLC, Elsevier, SirsiDynix) and include notes like 'Access recorded training videos with your LibApps account credentials.' and vendor support contacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect vendor platforms to have their own login flows, audience restrictions, and support channels; follow vendor instructions for account setup and technical help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic / content scope (subject matter to match needs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The guide lists many topical foci across providers: accessibility (SensusAccess, Library Accessibility Alliance), metadata/cataloging (Library of Congress Catalogers Workshop, NACO training), preservation (ALCTS Preservation Playlists, NEDCC Preservation Training), data management (RDMLA, ICPSR Data Fair), COUNTER/statistics (COUNTER Videos), vendor systems (SirsiDynix, ExLibris, EBSCO), pedagogy and instruction (Information Literacy Instruction), AI and tech topics (Generative AI, Text Analysis Pedagogy, coding), etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match the training topic to skill gaps (accessibility, preservation, metadata, data management, vendor systems, pedagogy, tech/AI). Review provider descriptions to confirm topic depth (introductory vs advanced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider-specific licensing or account linking (HR/LinkedIn Learning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some access is mediated by institutional arrangements: 'LinkedIn Learning: Access provided by Human Resources. Details available here.'; 'SpringShare (Libguides) Recorded Training — Access recorded training videos with your LibApps account credentials.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check with HR or library administration about institutional subscriptions (LinkedIn Learning, vendor portals) and any steps needed to link accounts or request access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider notes about free vs member-only content or requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Many entries include brief qualifiers such as 'Available to institutional members', 'Some content is free', or 'Not all events are free.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume universal free access; read provider notes carefully and confirm membership or payment requirements before planning attendance.
